short: Drops DTW from an EEG-to-Mel generator (M06, standard) but tests only the ten trained classes (M12, behind); one frozen ASR both trains and scores it, and EEG output beats recorded-speech WER.
position: The paper changes the decoder (M06): it regresses Mel spectrograms from trial-locked EEG without the DTW alignment and discriminator of its closest prior, NeuroTalk, and otherwise inherits NeuroTalk's spoken-audio targets, HuBERT-CTC loss, HiFi-GAN vocoder and spoken-to-imagined transfer. Regression is a common objective among EEG and MEG decoders, so M06 is standard, and no ablation tests the DTW removal; timing is fixed by the protocol instead. The evaluation (M12) is behind: voice reconstruction from imagined speech is shown only for the ten trained classes under a random split, while sentence-disjoint tests are the usual approach and NeuroTalk held out a word. The same frozen HuBERT recognizer gives the CTC training loss and scores the output, which, with reproduction of trained class templates, fits the 2-s result that EEG output scores better on WER (not CER) than that recognizer on the recorded speech. LLM correction (M07) is standard and gives small pooled gains.
